note: MC-11 program decisions, numbered continuously after D-040. Each decision states what it authorises and what it does not; no decision upgrades a commercial status, price, certification, compatibility or safety gate.

decisions.title: MC-11 is internal hardware feasibility only; formal procurement evidence stays blocked
decisions.context: The authoritative registry requires real supplier quotation evidence for milestone 11. No supplier could be contacted in MC-11 and no genuine quotation exists.
decisions.decision: Deliver a complete internal engineering feasibility package and report the milestone as PARTIAL: internal feasibility scope PASS, formal procurement evidence BLOCKED_OR_NOT_OBTAINED. Catalogue prices are classified as observations, never as quotations.
decisions.rationale: A missing quotation cannot be replaced by a distributor web price; the only honest way to satisfy the registry requirement is to record it as not obtained.
decisions.consequences: No BOM is production-approved, no price is approved and no procurement may start; MC-12 inherits per-line cost confidence and explicit quotation gaps.
decisions.statusEffect: MC11 verdict PARTIAL; no commercial status change.

decisions.title: No hardware architecture is frozen; HUB-D is the engineering preference and HUB-E is a commercial-strategy question
decisions.context: Scored candidates show the hybrid gateway (ARCH-HUB-D, 3.85) as the best proprietary engineering option while the software-first option (ARCH-HUB-E, 4.53) scores highest overall; DISPLAY size and architecture and AIS hardware posture are also open.
decisions.decision: Record all candidates as PROPOSED_NOT_APPROVED. Keep HUB-D as the engineering preference for a proprietary gateway, escalate the build-appliance-versus-integrate-certified-gateways choice (HUB-D vs HUB-E) as a commercial decision, and keep DISPLAY and AIS hardware unfrozen.
decisions.rationale: The weighted score measures engineering/operational fit, not commercial strategy, and no customer requirement exists to break the tie.
decisions.consequences: Gate G1 remains CANDIDATE_ONLY; no schematic, carrier board, tooling or supplier engagement may be started on the basis of this preference.
decisions.statusEffect: Architecture status PROPOSED_NOT_APPROVED; G1 not passed.

decisions.title: AIS transmitter development is prohibited; receive-only integration goes through third-party certified equipment
decisions.context: AIS is four different products (receive-only, third-party integration, transponder hardware, software visualisation). Radio transmission adds RED, spectrum, maritime approval and liability obligations that MC-11 cannot evaluate.
decisions.decision: Permit only receive-only data integration and software visualisation in the candidate portfolio; prohibit any AIS transmitter/transponder development; defer MAREA-branded AIS receiver hardware until a certified-module route is evaluated.
decisions.rationale: The conformity and liability burden of transmitting equipment is materially larger than its commercial value at this stage, and no approval route has been investigated.
decisions.consequences: AIS_TRANSMISSION_OFFERED = false; any future transmitter proposal needs a separate authorised programme, not an MC-11 extension.
decisions.statusEffect: AIS transmit capability prohibited; no product approval.

decisions.title: PILOT remains safety-blocked with a documented deferral disposition
decisions.context: PILOT has a hard safety gate. MC-11 produced a documentation-only safety feasibility analysis; no actuator, E-stop, redundancy or vessel test exists.
decisions.decision: Keep PILOT_SAFETY_GATE = BLOCKED and record the disposition DEFER_SAFETY_CRITICAL_DEVELOPMENT combined with REQUIRES_QUALIFIED_SAFETY_ENGINEERING and BLOCKED_PENDING_FUNDING_AND_TEST_PLAN. No control output, motor driver, steering command or firmware change is authorised.
decisions.rationale: A hardware BOM or a motor-driver component does not create safety evidence; qualified engineering, funded testing and insurance are prerequisites.
decisions.consequences: PILOT appears in no bundle line and no BOM is authorised for actuation; the safety case outline remains an outline.

decisions.title: Hardware price and claim grading rules adopted as binding for MC-11 and later milestones
decisions.context: Public catalogue prices, engineering estimates and assumptions are routinely confused with quotations, and component approvals are routinely confused with product conformity.
decisions.decision: Adopt the MC-11 evidence classes: every external figure is classified (manufacturer list price, authorised distributor, third-party reseller, historical observation, calculated estimate, engineering assumption, budgetary indication, unknown); a formal quotation requires a genuine attributable quotation; unknown is never zero; a non-EUR price converts only with a recorded rate; component-level conformity never becomes product-level conformity; compatibility is never TESTED or SUPPORTED without a recorded device test.
decisions.rationale: The economics and conformity conclusions are only useful if their evidence class is auditable and stable across milestones.
decisions.consequences: MC-12/MC-13 must reuse these classes; any artefact that violates one fails the deterministic validator.
decisions.statusEffect: Evidence grading enforced; no price approved.

decisions.title: RFQ packages are prepared but not sent; supplier engagement and purchasing remain unauthorised
decisions.context: MC-11 may prepare professional RFQ material but may not contact suppliers, create accounts, request quotations or buy samples.
decisions.decision: Keep all ten RFQ drafts at RFQ_DRAFT_PREPARED / RFQ_APPROVAL_REQUIRED / RFQ_NOT_SENT with SUPPLIER_NOT_CONTACTED and FORMAL_QUOTE_NOT_OBTAINED. Symbolically authorise nothing: G2, G3, G4 and G5 remain not authorised.
decisions.rationale: Supplier contact is a separate control requiring explicit programme-owner permission; conflating preparation with transmission would fabricate progress.
decisions.consequences: No quotation, MOQ, lead time, tooling price, warranty term or sample exists; MC-12 must plan around missing quotations.
decisions.statusEffect: No supplier contact, no purchase, no prototype procurement.

decisions.title: The MC-11 data contract and 54-check validator become the hardware evidence gate
decisions.context: MC-11 produced 18 machine-readable files and a large volume of engineering claims that must stay internally consistent after the milestone closes.
decisions.decision: Adopt docs/marea/hardware/data/DATA-CONTRACT.md as binding and scripts/check-marea-hardware.mjs (50 mandated integrity rules plus 4 structural checks, with adversarial negative tests) as the deterministic gate for MC-11 artefacts and their later updates.
decisions.rationale: Independent review cannot scale to hand-checking every cross-reference; a deterministic gate with negative tests makes fabrication and silent upgrades fail closed.
decisions.consequences: Any future change to hardware data must pass the gate; weakening a rule requires a new decision, a contract version and independent re-verification.
decisions.statusEffect: Validation gate active; no commercial or safety status change.

decisions.title: MC-11 delivers internal hardware feasibility and stays PARTIAL because no formal quotation exists
decisions.context: The registry requires hardware BOM, supplier quotations and a conformity plan, but MC-11 was authorised only for internal engineering and public-source research: no supplier contact, RFQ, purchase, prototype or certification. The evidence environment could not retrieve application/datasheet PDFs, so no datasheet was retrieved and verified parameters come from manufacturer HTML pages, recorded as a disclosed limitation.
decisions.decision: Deliver D1-D37 as an internal feasibility package and record the verdict as PARTIAL with MC11_FORMAL_PROCUREMENT_EVIDENCE = BLOCKED_OR_NOT_OBTAINED; keep every architecture, price, compatibility and conformity statement unapproved; apply the independent audit corrections and require the auditor to re-verify them before any internal-scope PASS is claimed.
decisions.rationale: A catalogue price is not a quotation and an internal design review is not a certification; reporting a full PASS would require fabricating supplier or laboratory evidence, which the milestone forbids.
decisions.consequences: No BOM is production-approved and no price is approved; gates G1-G7 remain closed; MC-12 inherits per-line cost confidence, labelled assumptions and quotation gaps; MC-13 inherits capital, tooling, certification and working-capital gaps; draft PR #18 remains stacked and unmerged.
decisions.statusEffect: No supplier contact, purchase, test, certification, price approval, publication, merge or deployment.
